questions.context:
MRI the Boon

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) also known as nuclear magnetic resonance imaging, is a scanning technique for creating detailed images of the human body.

During MRI, a person will be asked to lie on a movable table that will slide into doughnut shaped opening of the machine to scan a specific portion of your body. The machine itself will generate a strong magnetic field around the person and radio waves will be directed at the body. It generate images of parts of body that can't be seen with X-rays, CT scans or ultrasound. It can help doctors to see inside joints, cartilage, ligaments, muscles and tendons, which makes it helpful for detecting various sports injuries.

MRI is also used to examine internal body structures and diagnose a variety of disorders, such as strokes, tumors, spinal cord injuries and eye or inner ear problems. It is also widely used in research to measure brain structure and function. It doesn't emit any harmful radiations.
questions.stem: Which is the biggest benefit of MRI compared with other imaging techniques?

options.label: A
options.text: It can help doctors to see inside joints.

options.label: B
options.text: It used to examine internal body structure.

options.label: C
options.text: No risk of being exposed to radiation.
